title: Their affairs by consultation
hookLine: the believers conduct their affairs by consultation (42:38)

cards: Hudaybiya, near Mecca. The Prophet ﷺ has just signed a treaty that some of his companions find hard to accept. He tells them: get up, sacrifice your animals, and shave your heads.
There will be no 'umra, no visit to the Kaaba, this year. Nobody moves. He says it three times.
Still nobody. He goes into his tent, to his wife Umm Salama, and tells her what's happened. And she gives him advice that changes the afternoon.
Bukhari records it. First, though, the verse that gives this surah its name.

teach.b: Surah Ash-Shura, verse thirty-eight, part of a list describing the believers.
Pickthall: "And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them."
Look at the company consultation keeps: prayer on one side, giving on the other. Shura, consultation, sits right between them, as part of the description of a believer, not as a management tip.

teach.h: A MECCAN HABIT, BEFORE ANY STATE.
teach.b: And the surah is counted among those revealed in Mecca, before there was any Muslim state, any government, any council. Consultation was a habit of believers before there was anything to govern.

Back on day three hundred seventy-three, this path heard the Prophet told to consult his companions, even after a consultation went badly. Here, the believers do it with each other. Now, back to the tent at Hudaybiya.

teach.h: UMM SALAMA: GO OUT, SAY NOTHING.
teach.b: Umm Salama said: Messenger of Allah, do you want them to do it? Then go out, don't say a word to anyone, sacrifice your animal, and call your barber to shave your head. He did exactly that.
When the companions saw him, they got up, sacrificed, and began shaving each other's heads, so eagerly, the report says, that they almost hurt each other.
A prophet, receiving revelation, asked his wife what to do, and took her advice.
Scholars point to this as a model: consultation isn't a formality, and good counsel can come from the person right beside you.

how: Muslims treat shura, mutual consultation, as a value for families, communities and leadership; scholars have long debated how binding it is on leaders and what forms it should take.

o: a pledge of loyalty given to a new leader
a ruling council made up of elders only
consultation, deciding things by taking counsel

s: Surah Ash-Shura was revealed after the Muslims had a state
it's counted among the Meccan surahs, from before any Muslim government.
at Hudaybiya, the Prophet took his wife's advice
Umm Salama told him to act without a word, and the companions followed.
42:38 lists consultation between prayer and giving
establish worship, affairs by counsel, spend of what We provided.

games.q: at Hudaybiya, the Prophet has told his companions three times to sacrifice, and no one moves. Umm Salama is in the tent. what does he do?
o: give the order a fourth time.
ask Umm Salama, and take her advice.
games.why: he asked her. she said: go out, say nothing, and sacrifice. he did, and they all followed.

practice: Think of one decision coming up, small or large: dinner, a trip, a change at work, a weekend, and who else it touches. Picture really asking them before you've decided, and wonder what they might see that you don't.
Then rest, without carrying the decision alone.

wordCard.voice: Shura, consultation, the practice Ash-Shura names as part of being a believer, alongside prayer and giving. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: and their affair is consultation among them (42:38).

carryVoice: Your line: consult. In the verse, it sits between prayer and giving. Rest well; more tomorrow.

sources.q: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (Umm Salama's advice at Hudaybiya)
